FILRODENSWMB.Credits.D3Delaunay: Delaunay triangulation for the map's cells, bundled into one file with delaunator and robust-predicates
FILRODENSWMB.Credits.SimplexNoise: the terrain's noise, modified for speed, giving exactly the same values
FILRODENSWMB.Credits.Idiomorph: updates the studio's panels in place when they are redrawn
FILRODENSWMB.Credits.Pixi: the map canvas in the web version; in Foundry the module uses Foundry's own
FILRODENSWMB.Credits.Handlebars: the interface templates in the web version; in Foundry the module uses Foundry's own
FILRODENSWMB.Credits.DOMPurify: cleans SVG images picked or imported, so they can carry no script or outside links
FILRODENSWMB.Credits.Fflate: writes and reads the zip files of Back up all maps and Restore from backup
FILRODENSWMB.Credits.Three: development build, with its OrbitControls add-on, used by the 3D view
FILRODENSWMB.Credits.AzgaarNames: names the generated places and realms, ported to JavaScript with its own seeded randomness
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ReliefEmphasisHint: How strongly the light picks out land that rises gently over large areas, such as wide plains and long inland slopes. The terrain's heights don't change, only how it is lit.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintReferenceMove: Drag to move the reference image
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintReferenceResize: Shift+Scroll to resize the reference image
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintCropDraw: Drag to draw the crop area
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintCropMove: Drag inside the crop area to move it
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintCropResize: Drag a corner of the crop area to resize it
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintPlaceSpring: Click to place a river source
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintMoveSpring: Drag a river source to move it
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintDeleteSpring: Ctrl+Click a river source to delete it
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintMovePoint: Drag a point to move it
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintInsertPoint: Shift+Click a line to add a point
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintDeletePoint: Ctrl+Click a point to delete it
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintEditLine: Double-click a point to edit the line
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintSelectRegion: Click a region to paint it and open it in the inspector
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintRegionPaint: Drag to paint land into the region
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintRegionEraseShift: Shift+Drag to paint land into the region
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintRegionFill: Click to fill the outlined land with the region
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintRegionFillShift: Shift+Click a region to empty it
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintSelectRoute: Click a route to pick it and open it in the inspector
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintSelectFeature: Click a river or fault to open it in the inspector
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintSelectMask: Click a land mask to open it in the inspector
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintSelectDecoration: Click a decoration to open it in the inspector
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintEditRoute: Double-click a route to open it in the inspector
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintRouteFinish: Right-click, Enter or double-click to finish the route
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintRouteUndoWaypoint: Backspace or Ctrl+Z to take the last click or stroke back
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintRouteMoveWaypoint: Drag a waypoint to move it
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintRouteInsertWaypoint: Shift+Click the route to add a waypoint there
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintRouteRemoveWaypoint: Ctrl+Click a waypoint to remove it
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintRouteSplit: Alt+Click a waypoint to split the route there
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintRouteJoin: Alt+Drop an end waypoint on another route's end to join them
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintRouteTrace: Drag to trace a stretch of the route
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintFinishMask: Right-click to finish the land mask
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintMoveMask: Shift+Drag a point to move the whole land mask
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintEditMask: Double-click a point to edit the land mask
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintSelectPin: Click a pin to open it in the inspector
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintMovePin: Drag a pin to move it
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintResizePin: Hold a pin and Shift+Scroll to resize it
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintDeletePin: Ctrl+Click a pin to delete it
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintEditPin: Double-click a pin to open it in the inspector
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintSelectLabel: Click a label to open it in the inspector
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintMoveLabel: Drag a label to move it
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintRotateLabel: Hold a label and scroll to rotate it
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintResizeLabel: Hold a label and Shift+Scroll to resize it
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintEditLabel: Double-click a label to open it in the inspector
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintMoveDecoration: Drag a decoration or the scale bar to move it
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintRotateDecoration: Hold a decoration and scroll to rotate it
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintResizeDecoration: Hold a decoration and Shift+Scroll to resize it
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintEditDecoration: Double-click a decoration to edit it
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintDropMask: Release to drop the land mask
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ShortcutEscape: Escape to close a menu or dialog
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ShortcutRegionLetGo: Escape to let go of the active region
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ShortcutRegionStopStroke: Escape to end a stroke, or to let go of the active region
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ShortcutRouteLetGo: Escape to let go of the route being edited
FILRODENSWMB.UI.NextReasonScene: New map sets where land is; Terrain sets how it looks.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.NextReasonTerrain: Biomes read the terrain: settle sea level and relief first.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.NextReasonBiomes: Rivers follow the terrain and the moisture the biomes read.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.NextReasonFeatures: Generate settles the land the earlier tools have shaped.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.NextReasonRegions: Regions, routes and pins, and labels can be worked in any order.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.NextReasonInfrastructure: Every pin, route and region label is listed there too.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.NextReasonLabels: Cartography adds the scale bar, border, grid and decorations.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.NextReasonCartography: Export saves the map as an image or a Foundry scene.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.LatitudeHint: The latitudes of the map's top and bottom edges. They shape the climate, and so the biomes, and set how far the map spans from top to bottom.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RegionalMapCropHint: Choose Crop on the bar and drag on the map to mark the area.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.NoCustomBiomes: No custom biomes yet. Add one with + in this section's title.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.LabelLineWidthHint: Longest line, in characters, before the label wraps; 0 for no limit.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.SaveStyleAsHint: Make a style from these fields, and use it here
FILRODENSWMB.UI.InspectorApplyHint: Changes apply at once; each is one undo step.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.LabelFontsMissing: This map's labels use fonts this host lacks ({fonts}). They are drawn in {fallback} here, and keep their own font for a host that has it.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ExportPngHint: Saves the map as a PNG image, showing the layers the map controls have switched on, at a scale you choose (one is recommended so the smallest names can be read). The reference image and the land masks' outlines are left out.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ExportSceneHint: Creates a Foundry scene from the map, with its grid. The next step asks for the scene's name and folder, and whether to add journal entries.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.StretchTooltip: Higher values flatten valleys into continental shelves and push peaks higher.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.MapTransformHint: Nudge the camera to explore adjacent landmasses, or zoom out to generate larger, sweeping continents.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ThematicPopulationHint: How many people live on each area of land in the last generator run, blended between the run's cells.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ThematicCapacityHint: How many people the land could feed on each area, from its soil, climate, rivers and fishing, in the last generator run. Compare it with Population, on the same scale, to see where land is still free.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ThematicClearedHint: The share of the land cleared for fields and pasture rather than left wild, in the last generator run.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ThematicDangerHint: The share of the people lost to raiders and strife in the last generator run: highest on contested borders and far from towns and castles.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ThematicDangerUnit: share of the people lost to raiders and strife
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ThematicCultureHint: The culture most of the people belong to in the last generator run, in its color. The color is paler where several peoples live together.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ThematicNoCultures: Add a culture in Generate, then generate again, to see this layer.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ThematicTradeHint: The trade the last generator run carried, along its roads, rivers and sea lanes: the wider the line, the busier the route. It can be shown on its own or beside a color layer.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ThematicTradeUnit: Width by trade, against the busiest route
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ThematicNoRun: Generate this map to see these layers.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ThematicNoRunRegional: Generate this regional map, or cut it again from its map, to see these layers. This regional map was cut before regional maps carried their map's run.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ThematicInherited: From the run of the map this was cut from.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ThematicNeedsRerun: Generate again to see this layer: the last run was made before it existed.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ThematicStale: From the last run, which is out of date.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ThematicNeedsRerunAge: Generate again to see this age's peoples: the last run was made before they were kept.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HistoryAgesHint: Choose an age to see the map as it was then. The map shows it while this tool is open, with every age's roads drawn alike.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HistoryOneAge: The last run had one age, so the map has no past to show. Add ages in Generate, then generate again.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HistoryNoRun: Generate this map with more than one age to see its past.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HistoryRealmFellHint: Marked realms are gone by the present: no realm of today carries them on.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HistoryRealmFocus: Show this realm on the map
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HistoryPeoples: Share of the land by people
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HistoryExportHint: Saves the map as it was in this age as a PNG image, named with the age.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintSetTravelStart: Click the map to set where the journey starts
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ThematicTravelShown: The Travel tool's day bands are shown while it is open.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TravelStartHint: Click the map to choose where the journey starts; a click on a place starts there. The land is then colored by the days it takes to reach, with a line at the edge of each band, and the quickest way to the pointer is drawn with its time.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TravelStartMove: Click the map again to move the start.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TravelNoRoads: This map has no roads or sea routes, so the journey crosses the wilds and takes small boats. Draw routes, or generate the map, to travel by road, river and sea.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TravelModeHint: The way over land. Off the roads a mount or a wagon loses most of its lead over a walker. Rivers and the sea are crossed by boat and ship at their own speeds, whichever is chosen.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TravelSpeedsHint: A day's travel. Over land, each speed is on a road across level ground: off the road, forest and hills are slower, and farmland is quicker than the wilds. Ships keep to the map's sea routes and river boats to its river trade routes; elsewhere only small boats are found. Passage takes a few hours to find at a town's harbour and days elsewhere on the coast.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TravelIntervalHint: Each band and line marks this many days, up to ten bands. Automatic suits the map's size: a day on a small region, ten on a world.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TravelExportHint: Saves the map with this journey's day bands and lines as a PNG image, named with the way of travel and the start.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.SymbolSizeAutoHint: Pins and names grow with how closely the map shows its world, so a regional map's can be read at its scale. A top map is drawn at 100%.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.InspectorGeneratedHint: What the run that made it recorded. These figures are kept apart from the description.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.CulturesHint: Each culture spreads from its homelands through the land that suits it, and names its own places.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.CulturesNoneHint: With no cultures, one people lives everywhere and names its places in the Name style.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.CultureDeleteConfirm: Delete the culture {name}? Places already generated keep their names.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.CultureNameStyleHint: The language this culture's places and realms are named in.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.CultureOpennessHint: How readily this culture mixes with others. Open cultures blend over wide borderlands and draw others to their towns; closed ones keep sharp borders and keep others out.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.CultureDensityHint: How many people the same land feeds when this culture farms it, compared with other cultures.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.CultureHabitatHint: The land this culture suits. It spreads quickly and settles densely there, and slowly and thinly elsewhere. Double-click a track to remove its limit.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.CultureHeightHint: Elevation, from the sea level to the highest peaks, as the Elev readout shows it.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.CultureReliefHint: How rugged the land is: the difference in height across a small area, in the same units as Height.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.CultureCoastHint: Whether this culture seeks out the coast or keeps away from it.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.CultureRiverHint: Whether this culture seeks out rivers or keeps away from them.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.CultureHomelandsAuto: Auto: one is placed where the land suits this culture best, away from the other cultures.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.CultureHomelandsGivenHin: The culture spreads from all of these at once.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.CultureHomelandAddHint: Then click the map's land to add a homeland there. Escape stops.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.CultureHomelandOnWater: A homeland must be on land.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.CultureHomelandsFull: A culture can have at most {count} homelands.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintPlaceHomeland: Click land to add a homeland
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintStopHomeland: Escape to stop adding a homeland
FILRODENSWMB.UI.GenerateHomelandsLeftOut: Homelands of {name} not on land were left out: {count}.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.GenerateHomelandsPlacedN: No homeland of {name} is on land, so one was placed for it.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.GeneratedLockHint: A locked item is kept when you generate again, as one you have edited is. A region keeps its whole realm.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ListLockedHint: Locked: kept when you generate again. Click to unlock.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ListEditedHint: Edited, so kept when you generate again. Click to lock it as well.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ListUnlockedHint: Not locked. Click to lock it, so Generate again keeps it.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RiverMeanderHint: How much rivers meander where the land is flat. At 0 they never meander; above 1 they also meander on gentler slopes.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RiverWidthHint: Scales how wide every river is drawn. Rivers still start narrow and widen as tributaries join them.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.AreaFactorHint: How much smaller the world is than its latitudes alone would make it. The map's latitudes set its height; the area factor divides the world's area by this number, so a continent spanning most of the map has the size of a believable medieval realm rather than a whole Earth. It sets what a pixel measures (shown below it, in the map unit) for every distance the module works out from the map's scale, such as how far apart settlements and routes are when they are generated. Nothing drawn changes, except a scale bar set to match the world. 15 is the default; 1 is a true-to-latitude world.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.MapUnitHint: The name of the unit every distance on this map is shown in: the scale bar, territorial waters, the thematic layers and the line below. The module measures distances in kilometers and shows the number with this name, so the figures are true kilometers whatever the unit is called. Change it to give the unit your world's own name.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.MapUnitConverted: This map's scale bar used the old default unit, Miles, for distances the module measures in kilometers. Its map unit is now km (in New map, under Generation). Save the map to keep the change.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ExportSettingsHint: Bundle your custom biomes and styles into a shareable file.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ExportSettingsNoneSelect: Select at least one category to export.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ImportSettingsHint: Load custom biomes and styles shared by another GM.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ImportSettingsSuccessWit: Imported {count} item(s) into this map ({duplicates} already present, skipped).
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ImportSettingsAllDuplica: Every item in that file is already in this map's styles. Nothing new to import.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ImportSettingsEmpty: That file didn't contain any recognized custom biomes or styles.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ImportSettingsError: Failed to import settings. Please check the file and try again.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ReliefShadingHint: Shades slopes as if lit from the north-west, so hills, valleys and seabed features stand out, with or without biomes. Set to 0 to turn off.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.SeabedReliefHint: How much of the relief shading still shows through deep water. At 0 the sea floor's shape fades with depth; at 1 its ridges and trenches stay as sharp as on land.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.WaterHueHint: The hue of the sea and lakes, from blue-green through blue to blue-violet. Depth still decides how light or dark the water is.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.WaterClarityHint: How deep you can see into the water. Higher values show more of the seabed and its biomes further from the shore.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.NoCustomStyles: No styles yet. Add one below, or with Save as… in an object's inspector.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.InspectorStyleApplyHint: Changes apply at once, to the style and everything that uses it; each is one undo step.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.StyleTransportHint: The routes this style is offered for: a road style to roads, a sea style to sea routes, a river style to river routes, and a style for any transport to all of them. Routes already using it keep it.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.StyleDeleteUsedOne: 1 {one} uses {name}; it keeps its look as Custom.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.StyleDeleteUsed: {count} {many} use {name}; they keep its look as Custom.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ListNoMatches: Nothing matches the search and filters.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.MassDeleteHint: Deletes everything chosen in this list, as one undo step.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.MassDeletePins: Delete {count} pins? One undo step brings them back.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.MassDeleteRoutes: Delete {count} routes? One undo step brings them back.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.MassDeleteLabels: Delete {count} labels? One undo step brings them back.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.MassEditHint: A field changes only if you change it. Fields marked Mixed differ between the chosen items; ↺ puts a field back.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.BuiltinPinIconsHint: Hide icons you don't use to keep the picker tidy. The default pin icon can't be hidden.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.PinIconProtected: This is the default pin icon and can't be hidden
FILRODENSWMB.UI.NoCustomPinIcons: No custom pin icons yet. Add one with + in this section's title.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.PinIconWhiteCheckHint: Custom pin icons must be solid white on a transparent background to render correctly. Check the preview above before accepting.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RemovePinIconConfirm: Remove the custom icon "{name}"? This only removes it from the picker (the SVG file itself won't be touched).
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RemovePinIconInUseWarnin: "{name}" is currently used by {count} pin(s). Removing it will change those pins to the default icon. This only removes the icon from the picker (the SVG file itself won't be touched). Continue?
FILRODENSWMB.UI.UnresolvedPinIconsWarnin: {count} pin(s) on this map use custom icons that aren't available here, and show the default icon instead.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.FlatTextureHint: Gives the new Flat map a fine, natural texture instead of perfectly flat ground. Smooth removes it and Roughen puts it back. Applies when you select Create new map.
FILRODENSWMB.Web.StorageUnavailable: This browser is not letting the map builder store anything, so saved maps will be lost when the page closes. Export maps you want to keep.
FILRODENSWMB.Web.StartFailed: The map builder could not start: {detail}
FILRODENSWMB.UI.GridDataSizeMismatch: The exported scene's grid is not the size its grid data was worked out for, so the grid data will not match the scene's grid cells. See the console for details.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.SaveError: The map couldn't be saved. In Foundry, check that the module's compendium is unlocked.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.PreparingMapMigrate: Preparing map: migrating regions and routes…
FILRODENSWMB.UI.MapUpgraded: This map's regions and routes have been converted to the new format. Save the map to keep the conversion.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.MeshRebuilt: This map's mesh no longer matched the map and has been rebuilt. Check its regions and routes, then save the map.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.MeshOwnersLost: Some regions could not be restored and are now empty: {detail}
FILRODENSWMB.UI.MeshLoadFailed: This map's regions and routes could not be prepared. They are kept as they were saved and are not shown.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RegionModeSelect: Select: click a region to paint it and open it in the inspector
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RegionModePaint: Paint land into the region (Shift: erase)
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RegionModeErase: Erase any region under the brush (Shift: paint)
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RegionModeFill: Fill: click to give the region the connected land shown (Shift: take that land back out of its region)
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ShowAllLevelsHint: While painting, only the layer being painted and the layers above it are drawn. Turn this on to draw every layer and set as the map shows them.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.WarnNoActiveRegion: Choose a region to paint (click one on the map or in the Regions panel), or add a new one.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.WarnOutsideParent: Start painting inside a region of the parent layer: this layer's regions stay inside their parent regions.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ChildCellsCleared: {count} cells of the layers below are now unassigned, since the ground above them changed region. Auto-assign cells in a layer's menu can fill them again.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.DeleteLevelConfirm: Delete the layer {name}? Its {regions} regions and {cells} painted cells go with it, and the {childLevels} layers below it move up to its parent.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.LayerSetsHint: A new layer set: one way of dividing the map (for example political or climate), shown over the map on its own.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.DeleteLayerSetConfirm: Delete the layer set {name}? Its {levels} layers and {regions} regions go with it.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.LayerSetOpacityHint: Multiplies the fill opacity of every layer in the set, so the whole set can be faded without changing the balance between its layers.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.LayerSetWaterTintHint: Shows a faint fill where the set's regions claim water. Off, regions are filled over land only.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.NestingFreeHint: Free nesting: this layer's regions may cross the borders of its parent layer's regions.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.NestingProblemsHint: {count} cells lie outside their region's parent region. Fix nesting in the layer's menu repairs them.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.AddLayerHint: A new layer below, named by its tier until you rename it. Its regions sit inside the regions of the layer above.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ChooseParentRegion: Choose a region in {name} to see its regions.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.UnassignedHint: Regions without a single parent region (free nesting, or painted before parents were kept).
FILRODENSWMB.UI.NameNewSet: Name of the new layer set
FILRODENSWMB.UI.AutoAssignHint: Gives the unassigned land inside each parent region to the nearest of this layer's regions in that parent.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.AutoAssigned: {count} cells assigned to the regions of {name}.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.FixNestingHint: Gives each region the parent region holding most of its cells, and unassigns its cells outside that parent.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.LevelTitleTemplateHint: How a region's title reads at this layer, with {name} standing for the region's name (for example "Kingdom of {name}"). The map builder records it for the generator and for other modules; labels show the region's name.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.LevelNestingHint: Constrained: a region is painted only inside its parent region, and painting a parent region clears the child cells it takes. Free: regions may cross their parent's borders.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.LevelWatersHint: How far this layer's regions claim the sea from their coasts, in the map unit. Water goes to the nearest region, so neighbors meet halfway; a lake with one region on all its shores is wholly that region's. At 0 regions own land only. The waters follow every stroke.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.LevelScaleWithMapHint: Off, border thicknesses are map pixels. On, they grow and shrink with the map's resolution, as pins and labels do.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.WarnNoLevel: Add a layer before adding regions.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RegionsHint: A new region in this list, ready to paint.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.MergeRegionHint: The cells of {name} join the region chosen below, and {name} is removed.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.MergeNoOther: This layer has no other region to merge into.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.DeleteConfirm: Are you sure you want to delete this?
FILRODENSWMB.UI.NoPoints: No pins yet. Choose Place on the bar, then click the map.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.NoRoutes: No routes yet. Choose Route and Draw on the bar, then click the map.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.Name: Name
FILRODENSWMB.UI.PinStyleHint: A named look for a kind of place: its icon, color and size, and its label's size and visibility. A pin made with a style follows the style when it is edited. Pin styles are managed in Styles and icons.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.PinStyleLabelHint: What the label of a pin made with this style starts with. A label style sets its font, color, width and alignment; the size here is used over the label style's own.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.PinNameLevelHint: The detail level from which the names of pins with this style are shown, chosen with Detail in the map controls. A name never shows before its pin, and a label set to hidden stays hidden.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.PinDetailLevelHint: The detail level from which pins with this style are shown, chosen with Detail in the map controls. Pins at World are shown at every level.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.NextRouteStyleHint: The style the next route drawn gets. A route's own look is changed in its inspector.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.NextLabelStyleHint: The style the next label placed gets. A label's text and look are changed in its inspector.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RouteLegModeHint: How the legs between waypoints are found. Follow terrain finds the easiest way for the transport, avoiding steep ground and keeping to the ground it can use. Straight joins the waypoints directly.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RouteTransportHint: What travels the route, chosen when it is drawn. Roads keep to land and prefer to join existing roads; sea routes keep to water.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RouteTransportFixedHint: Chosen when the route was drawn. A road's waypoints are all on land and a sea route's all on water, so a finished route cannot change transport.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RouteSpanWaterHint: Lets a Follow terrain road cross water between its waypoints, as a bridge, causeway or ferry, at a steep cost per cell of water: it bridges a strait when going round would be longer and keeps to land otherwise. It can only bridge water about twelve cells wide; wider water needs a sea route. Its waypoints must still be on land. Applies to legs found from now on; Re-path in the inspector applies it to a finished route.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RouteDetailHint: How closely a traced stroke is kept, in map cells. A bend becomes a waypoint when the stroke strays further than this from the line between the bends either side of it, and a long run without a bend gains waypoints along it so the route keeps near the stroke. 1 keeps every bend; higher values keep fewer waypoints and leave more to the path finding.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RouteDetailEditorHint: Used by Simplify: a waypoint is dropped when it lies within this many map cells of the line between its neighbors. The same setting as Detail on the bar.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RouteClassHint: The route's importance, for other modules and the exported data. It does not change how the route is drawn.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RouteOutlineHint: Draws a thin dark edge along both sides of the line, so it stands out from the map.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RouteSmoothingHint: Rounds the corners of the line where it turns from cell to cell.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.WarnRouteUnreachable: That waypoint cannot be reached from the last one: a road keeps to land (bridging only narrow water when Span water is on) and a sea route to water.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.WarnRouteStrokeSkipped: {count} bends of the stroke could not be reached (off the route's ground, or across water it cannot bridge) and were left out.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.LabelNoRoomHint: There is no room for this name among the others, so it is not drawn. Drag it into place in the Labels tool, where it shows faintly, or turn off Avoid overlaps in the Detail menu.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.NoLabels: No labels yet. Choose Place on the bar, then click the map.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ScaleMatchWorldHint: Works out the value per major tick from the map's latitudes and area factor, rounded to 1, 2 or 5 of the map unit times a power of ten, and draws each tick as long as that distance is, close to the interval you set. Off, the interval and value are your own. The bar's unit is the map unit, set in New map under Generation.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.NoDecorations: No decorations yet. Add one with Add decoration on the bar.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.UnsavedChangesWarning: You have unsaved changes. Do you want to save your map before closing?
FILRODENSWMB.JOURNAL.Title: World map parameter log
FILRODENSWMB.JOURNAL.Description: This journal contains the full generation profile and mathematical vectors used during world creation. This allows you to see the complete settings for the model without having to load it.
FILRODENSWMB.JOURNAL.StandardPalette: No custom biome colors applied. Standard palette active.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.SceneNameHint: The name of the new Scene that will be created in your world.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ExportFolderHint: The folder inside your world directory where the map images will be saved.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.GenerateJournalsHint: Creates a Journal Entry for this map with a page for each named or described pin, route and region (whatever their visibility, since the journal is for the GM), linked to the Scene by map notes.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.CreateGMOverlayHint: Generates a transparent second tile holding everything set to GM only, invisible to players by default.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.OverwriteJournalsHint: If checked, existing map journals will be updated with your current descriptions. Warning: This will destroy any manual lore edits made by the GM.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HelpCopyVersionHint: Copies the module's version, the host, the browser, its WebGL and the map's size, for a bug report.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HelpCreditsIntro: The module includes this code, these icons and these fonts, each under its own license.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HelpCopyFailed: The version details could not be copied.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.DeleteBiomeConfirm: Are you sure you want to delete this custom biome? Any existing areas on the map will return to their original biomes.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.BiomeCodeHint: Optional, e.g. a system's terrain code
FILRODENSWMB.UI.BiomeBehavesLikeHint: How Generate treats this biome's land: how well it farms, how hard it is to cross, and how much cover it gives. By default it behaves as the biome the climate would give there.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.BiomePlacementHint: Where this biome can appear. Painting and auto-generation rules only place it there, and it is never shown anywhere else. Underwater biomes lie on the bed of the sea or a lake, seen through the water. Overwater biomes sit on top of the water, such as pack ice.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.PreviewFallbackCoverageH: Preview rule coverage: hover to highlight every area currently using a default biome rather than one of your custom rules.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RuleEditorIntro: Rules run top to bottom: the first range a pixel's elevation, moisture and temperature all fall inside wins. Defaults sit permanently at the bottom as a guaranteed fallback and can't be reordered or edited.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RuleEditorLegendOverlap: Ranges on the same axis are allowed to overlap.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RuleEditorLegendSeaLevel: The dashed line on Elevation is sea level, shown for reference. Custom ranges can cross it freely, including to define water biomes.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RuleEditorNoRulesYet: No auto-generation rules yet, so this biome will only appear where it's hand-painted.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RuleEditorDefaultsHint: Read-only, shown for reference so new rules can fit around or combine these.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RuleEditorSeaLevelToolti: Sea level (for reference only; ranges aren't restricted by it)
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RuleEditorAddIndependent: Adds another, separate rule for this biome, matched independently of the rows above it.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.GenerateSeedHint: What the settlements, routes and realms are made from. Left empty, the map's own seed is used. The same seed and settings always give the same result.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.GenerateNameStyleHint: The language the names of places and realms sound like.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.GenerateEstimateHint: A guide for a typical computer. A map that covers a larger area takes longer.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.GenerateLongRun: This will take a while. The map can't be used until it finishes, but you can cancel at any point.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.GenerateOutOfDateHint: The terrain, climate, rivers or area factor have changed since the last run. Generate again to bring the realms and settlements up to date.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.GenerateInheritedNotice: This regional map holds generated content from the map it was cut from. Generating here replaces it (except what you have edited or locked) with a run made for this map. To keep it and add villages and market towns between its places, use Fill in.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.GenerateSmallWorldNotice: This map covers a small area, so it gets only a few realms and the larger settlements. A larger area factor (in New map) makes the world larger, with more of them.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.GenerateRunHint: Makes settlements, routes and realms for this map. Generating again replaces what the last run made, except what you have edited or locked. One undo step takes a run back.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.GenerateAgainMessage: Generating again replaces what earlier runs made: {realms} realms, {places} places and {routes} routes. The {kept} you have edited or locked are kept (a region with its whole realm), as is everything you made by hand.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RemoveGeneratedHint: Removes the realms, places and routes Generate made, except those you have edited or locked. One undo step.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RemoveGeneratedMessage: This removes {realms} realms, {places} places and {routes} routes made by Generate. The {kept} you have edited or locked are kept (a region with its whole realm), as is everything you made by hand.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RemoveGeneratedNothing: There is no generated content to remove: what is left you have edited or locked.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.GenerateAgesHint: The history the map grows through, oldest first. Each age starts from the one before; the last is the present, and is what the map shows.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.GenerateEraHint: How much of the land is farmed, and whether a great plague has thinned the people.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.GenerateStrifeHint: How dangerous the borders and the wild are: more strife means more castles and walled towns, and fewer people where it is unsafe.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.GenerateEventHint: A culture that arrives in this age is absent from the ages before. One that invades also takes land from the peoples it meets, and the age is more war-torn there.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.GenerateAgesStoppedNotic: The last run stopped after {run} of {asked} ages.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.GenerateDensityHint: How many people the land feeds, as a multiple of the usual. Higher values give more and larger settlements.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.GenerateUrbanizationHint: The share of people living in towns and cities, as a multiple of the usual. Higher values give larger towns and busier roads.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.GenerateRealmSpacingHint: How far apart royal seats must be, as a multiple of the usual. Higher values give fewer, larger realms; lower values more, smaller ones.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.GenerateFragmentationHin: How far a lord's wealth carries his rule. Above 1 the map breaks into more, smaller duchies and realms; below 1 fewer, larger ones hold together.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.GenerateLevelsHint: Realms are always made. Duchies and counties are layers below them in the Political set.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.GeneratePlacesHint: Capitals are always placed. Fortified towns and ports count by their size.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.GenerateHistoryHint: What the age before the present left: the ruins of its towns, its abandoned castles and the roads no one uses now. Former capitals take their own style.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.GenerateLabelsHint: Shows the names of the places, realms and routes the run makes, each from its style's name detail level (see Detail in the map controls). Off, every place is still named, with its label hidden.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.GenerateDefaultStylesHin: Sets the pin, label and route styles that generated content uses back to their defaults before the run, keeping their names, and restyles everything that follows them. On at first when this map's styles are from an earlier version and suit a different scale.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.InfillHint: Adds villages and market towns between the places this regional map inherited, joined to them by lanes, from the people of the map it was cut from. What it inherited stays as it is. Villages and market towns stand only near the roads, river routes and towns the map inherited, and the area factor (in New map) sets how many show: the larger it is, the fewer villages and the further apart the market towns. Market towns and villages of 1,000 people or more show from the Local detail level, the other villages at Everything.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.InfillTooCoarse: This regional map is too far out to fill in. Cut a regional map closer in to add villages and market towns.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.InfillNoParentRun: This regional map holds no copy of the run of the map it was cut from. Cut it again from that map to fill it in.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.InfillRunHint: Adds villages, market towns and lanes. Filling in again replaces what the last fill-in added, except what you have edited or locked. One undo step takes it back.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.InfillNotReady: The map is still being prepared. Try again in a moment.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.InfillWorking: Filling in villages and market towns…
FILRODENSWMB.UI.InfillFailed: The villages and market towns could not be filled in.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.InfillDone: Filled in {markets} market towns and {villages} villages.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.InfillAgainMessage: Filling in again replaces the {count} villages, market towns and lanes the last fill-in added, except those you have edited or locked. What the map inherited stays as it is.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RegionalInfill: Fill in villages and market towns
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RegionalInfillHint: Fills in the regional map when you first open it (see Fill in, in the Generate tool). Offered once the regional map is close enough in.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.NextReasonGenerate: Refine the realms the generator made, or draw your own.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.GenerateNotReady: The map is still being prepared. Try again in a moment.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.GenerateFailed: The settlements, routes and realms could not be generated.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.NoFaultLines: No fault lines yet. Choose Fault on the bar, then click the map.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.FaultStyleHint: Simple raises and enlarges the land's own hills and valleys. Fold belt lays long parallel ridges along the range. Rugged cuts sharp ridges and valleys running down from the crest.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.FaultThicknessHint: How far the feature spreads from its line, in pixels. For a mountain range, rift or subduction zone this is its width either side of the line; for a hotspot chain it is the width of the band its islands lie in, and a young island is about a third of it.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.FaultStrengthHint: How pronounced the feature is: the height of a mountain range or of a subduction zone's volcanic arc, the depth of a rift, or the height of a hotspot chain's youngest volcanoes above sea level.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.FaultArcDistanceHint: How far from the trench the chain of volcanoes rises, as a share of the width. The volcanoes stand on the left side of the direction the line was drawn in.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.FaultTrenchDepthHint: How deep the trench along the line cuts into the seabed.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.FaultFloorTextureHint: How rough the rift floor is: 0 leaves smooth sediment, 1 adds young lava fields and small fault blocks.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.FaultVolcanoesHint: How many volcanoes rise on the rift floor and its shoulders. Set to 0 for none.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.FaultSpacingHint: The typical distance between volcanoes, in island sizes. Low values merge neighboring volcanoes into larger islands.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.FaultSpacingTrendHint: Negative values crowd the volcanoes closer together towards the young end of the chain; positive values spread them further apart, as if the plate sped up.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.FaultScatterHint: How far volcanoes stray either side of the line.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.FaultVariationHint: How much island sizes and the gaps between them vary. At 0 every island is the typical size and evenly spaced.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.FaultPulsesHint: How much the hotspot's output rises and falls along the chain. High values give clusters of large islands separated by long empty stretches.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.FaultVentsHint: How often extra volcanoes grow on an island's flanks, merging into one larger island.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.FaultDrownedHint: The share of the chain, from its oldest end, that has sunk below the sea as atolls and seamounts.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.FaultReverseHint: When ticked, the feature runs from the last point drawn to the first: a subduction zone's volcanoes rise on the right side of the line as drawn instead of the left side, and a hotspot chain's youngest volcano is at its first point instead of its last.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.NoManualRivers: No rivers drawn yet. Choose River on the bar, then click the map.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.PromoteConfirm: Make a standalone copy of this regional map? The copy is no longer listed under the map it was cut from.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RegionalGenerationError: The regional map couldn't be made.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ExportNoMap: There's no map to export yet.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ExportPngFailed: The PNG couldn't be made. The map may be larger than your graphics card can export.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ExportPngReasonNone: No names are shown, so the map's own size is enough.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ExportPngReasonEnough: The smallest names shown are {px} px tall, so the map's own size is enough to read them.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ExportPngReasonReaches: The smallest names shown are {px} px tall at 1×; {scale}× makes them {scaledPx} px, enough to read.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ExportPngReasonShort: The smallest names shown are {px} px tall at 1×; the largest scale this map allows, {scale}×, makes them {scaledPx} px. A larger Symbol size in the Detail menu makes them bigger.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ExportStepGridData: Working out the grid cell data…
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ExportSceneFailed: The scene export failed. The browser console has the details.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ImportError: That file isn't a map this module can import.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ImportCorrected: {count} values in the file weren't valid and were set to their defaults.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ImportRefusedTooLarge: This file can't be imported: it's larger than an import can be.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ImportRefusedNotMap: This file can't be imported: it isn't a map saved by the World Map Builder.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ImportRefusedNotStyles: This file can't be imported: it isn't a styles file saved by the World Map Builder.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ImportRefusedDamaged: This file can't be imported: its map data is damaged.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ImportRefusedTextTooLong: This file can't be imported: the {field} of {what} is {length} characters long, and the limit is {limit}.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ImportRefusedMore: {count} more texts are over their limits too.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ImportRefusedImage: This image can't be used: it must be a PNG, JPEG, WebP or SVG image of at most {megabytes} MB and {pixels} pixels on each side.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ImageSourceInvalid: This image can't be used: choose an image file, or give the path of one in your data.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ExportRefusedIntro: This map can't be exported, because these texts are longer than an export allows. Shorten them, then export again.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ImportRefusedNotBackup: This file can't be restored: it isn't a backup made by the World Map Builder.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ImportImagesLeftOut: {count} images in the file couldn't be used and were left out.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.BackUpAllMapsHint: Saves every map, with the images and custom pin icons it uses, in one zip file for you to keep.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RestoreFromBackupHint: Adds maps from a backup file as new saved maps. Nothing already saved is changed.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.BackupNoMaps: There are no saved maps to back up.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.BackupLargeContent: This backup is about {size} MB, most of it images. Back up everything, or only the maps without their images?
FILRODENSWMB.UI.BackupImagesLeftOut: {count} images couldn't be read and were left out of the backup.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.BackupFailed: The backup failed. The browser console has the details.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RestoreIntro: Choose the maps to restore. Each is added as a new saved map; a map marked Already saved is added as a copy, which you can review and delete.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RestoreSummaryCopies: These maps were already saved, so they were added as copies:
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RestoreSummaryImages: {count} images couldn't be used and were left out.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.PauseTerrainGeneration: Pause automatic terrain generation (use the Apply button to regenerate the terrain yourself)
FILRODENSWMB.UI.DrawLandMaskHint: Draw areas of the map that could be land.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.DrawOceanMaskHint: Draw areas of the map that could be ocean.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RandomLandMaskHint: Add a random shape of the selected type. Ocean shapes are always placed over existing land.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RandomLandMaskNoLand: There is no land on the map for a random Ocean shape to cut into.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RandomLandMapHint: Add a random map of land and sea: landmasses as Land shapes, with Ocean shapes for the lakes and seas inside them.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.NoLandMasks: No land masks yet. Choose Land or Ocean on the bar, then draw on the map.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.DeleteAllLandMasksHint: Delete every land mask drawn on this map.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.DeleteAllLandMasksConfir: Are you sure you want to delete all {count} land masks from this map?
FILRODENSWMB.UI.EngineStandardHint: Uses standard noise generation to create quick, randomized terrain.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.EngineFlatHint: Creates a completely flat landmass at sea level, acting as a blank canvas for manual terrain brushing.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.EngineAdvancedHint: Simulates tectonic plate collisions to build realistic continents, deep trenches, and mountain ridges.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.EngineGuidedHint: Uses your hand-drawn vector masks to dictate exact landmass and ocean placements.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TectonicPlatesHintV2: Controls the number of tectonic plates. Each plate is either buoyant continental crust or sinking ocean floor, so the plates decide where the continents lie. Where plates collide they raise mountain ranges on land and trenches at sea; where they pull apart they open rift valleys on land and mid-ocean ridges at sea.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.OceanRidgesHintTectonic: How high the mid-ocean ridges rise from the deep ocean floor. Ridges form where tectonic plates pull apart under the ocean, and fade out towards the continental slopes. Set to 0 for a flat ocean floor.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TectonicPlatesHint: Controls the number of shifting plates. Higher values create more frequent mountain ridges and fault-line valleys across the landmass, but will not significantly alter the global coastline.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.CoastlineFractureHint: Bends and distorts the edges of the continents. Higher values create undulating bays and  peninsulas, while lower values keep landmasses rounder and smoother.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ContinentalGroupingHint: Adjusts the baseline grouping of land. Higher values flood the map; lower values merge landmasses together.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.SurfaceRoughnessHint: Adds high-frequency detail. Low values create rolling hills; high values create jagged, rocky peaks.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ErosionScaleHint: Zooms the detail noise. Lower values cluster mountains tightly; higher values stretch features across broader areas.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ContinentScaleHint: How far inland the land takes to reach its full height, beyond the Coastal plains. Lower values create steep coastal mountains; higher values create broad, gradual slopes. Islands smaller than this rise over their own size instead, so they still have hills. Measured in pixels of a 1000 pixel map and scaled to your map's size, so the same value looks the same at any resolution.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.OceanRidgesHint: How high the mid-ocean ridges rise from the deep ocean floor. Ridges run down the middle of the ocean between continents, where the seabed is equally far from both, and fade out towards the continental slopes. Small islands do not create ridges. Set to 0 for a flat ocean floor.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.OceanScaleHint: How far out the seabed takes to fall to the deep ocean floor, beyond the Continental shelf. Lower values create abrupt drops into deep water; higher values create broad, gradual slopes and shallower seas between nearby coasts. Measured in pixels of a 1000 pixel map and scaled to your map's size.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ContinentScaleHintLegacy: Defines the gradient slope. Lower values create steep coastal mountains; higher values create sprawling, flat coastal plains.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ShelfRangeHint: Controls the width of the shallow water transition zone before dropping into deep ocean.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ShelfWidthHint: Width of the band of shallow sea along the coast, beyond which the seabed falls steeply to the deep ocean floor. Set to 0 for coasts that drop straight into deep water. Each 0.1 is 10 pixels on a 1000 pixel map, scaled to your map's size.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.CoastalPlainsHint: Width of the band of low, gently rolling land along the coast before the land starts to rise. Set to 0 to let the terrain rise straight from the shore. Each 0.1 is 10 pixels on a 1000 pixel map, scaled to your map's size.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TerrainUpdateIntro: This regional map was created with older terrain rules. Updating it makes it match its parent map more closely:
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TerrainUpdateTerrain: Finer terrain detail, such as more intricate coastlines. The overall shape of the land stays the same.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TerrainUpdateFaults: Fault lines and hotspot chains at the same size as on the parent map. They were narrower than on the parent, with their texture and volcanoes drawn at a different scale; they are widened to their width on the parent and drawn at its scale.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TerrainUpdateBiomes: Biomes that match the parent map. Rain shadows were placed too far downwind, so some forests, grasslands and deserts will move. Biome borders also gain finer detail.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TerrainUpdateNotSaved: The update is not saved automatically. Reloading the map without saving returns it to how it was. Saving the map keeps the update.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TerrainUpdateDismiss: Don't ask again for this map
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TerrainUpdateDismissHint: You can still update this map later with the update button at the top of the New map tool.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TerrainUpdateApplied: Map updated. Save the map to keep the update, or reload it to return to the original.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.UpdateMapHint: This map was created with older terrain rules. Update it to use the latest terrain engine.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TerrainUpdateIntroTecton: This map was created with the original tectonic engine (Advanced (tectonics) v1). Updating it to Advanced (tectonics) v2 builds the map's terrain with a new engine, so it will look completely different:
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TerrainUpdateTectonicsLa: The continents, coastlines, mountain ranges and oceans are built afresh from the same seed and settings. Nothing of the current layout is kept: land may become sea and sea may become land.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TerrainUpdateTectonicsFe: Everything placed on the map (pins, routes, regions, labels, rivers and terrain brush strokes) stays exactly where it is, so it may no longer fit the new land. Only update a map you are happy to rework.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TerrainUpdateIntroCoastl: This map was created with older terrain rules. Updating it to the latest guided terrain engine changes it as follows:
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TerrainUpdateFracture: Coastal fracture is lowered from {before} to {after}, which keeps your coastline close to its current shape. From now on, the same value gives the same look on a map of any size.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TerrainUpdateCoastlines: Coastal fracture and Continent scale used to be fixed sizes in pixels, so they had less effect the larger the map. They are now scaled to the map's size, so the same values look the same at any resolution, and coastlines gain finer detail.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TerrainUpdateProfile: Oceans become deeper. Continental shelf now sets the width of a band of shallow sea along the coast, beyond which the seabed falls steeply to the deep ocean floor. The new Coastal plains setting adds a band of low land along the coast. Continent scale now only sets how steeply the land rises, and the new Ocean scale (starting at your current Continent scale) sets how steeply the sea deepens. Small islands now rise to proper hills, and mid-ocean ridges rise between continents (see the new Mid-ocean ridges setting). The land masks you drew stay the same.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TerrainUpdateIntroFaults: This map was created with older terrain rules. Updating it changes its fault lines as follows:
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TerrainUpdateFeatures: Fault lines become the new tectonic features: convergent faults become mountain ranges, divergent faults become rifts, and hotspot chains become the new hotspot chains, running from their oldest volcano to their youngest. They look different, and you can adjust them afterwards.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TerrainUpdateSlip: Slip faults are removed, since the new tectonic features have no equivalent.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TerrainUpdateIntroRivers: This map was created with older river rules. Updating it changes its rivers as follows:
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TerrainUpdateRivers: Rivers follow the lie of the land more closely instead of running in straight lines, a river that runs beside another joins it, and a lake that fills up breaks out through its lowest shore so its river flows on. River sources are placed afresh from the land and climate (the ones you added yourself are kept), so many rivers take a different course, and some lakes move, grow or shrink.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TerrainUpdateChannels: Custom rivers run exactly along the line you drew, carry on downhill from its end, and are drawn like any other river. The ground around each is lowered into a gentle valley that keeps the texture of the land, in place of the old channel.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RegionalMapNeedsUpdate: This map was created with older terrain rules. Update it to the latest engine (see the New map tool) to create regional maps from it.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RegionalMapSaveFirstNew: This map has not been saved yet. A regional map is listed under the map it was created from, so save this map first. Save it now and create the regional map?
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RegionalMapSaveFirstChan: This map has unsaved changes. A regional map is created from the map as you see it, so save the changes first to keep the saved map and its regional map matching. Save now and create the regional map?
